subject: seagulls
one_liner: Territory-verified matchmaking for gulls who are done circling.
brand_voice_notes: A sincere founder pitch that never notices it is about seagulls. Port-authority vocabulary throughout: attestation, provenance, tide cycles, notice to mariners. The absurdity is carried by specificity (slip numbers, decibel peaks, witness counts), never by winking.

hero.sub: Keel matches herring gulls on verified territory, call spectrogram, and documented theft history. The pier is crowded. Your standards shouldn't be.

features.title: Territory Attestation
features.blurb: Every profile is pinned to one verified perch. We cross-reference municipal boardwalk records and tide schedules so nobody claims a dumpster they can't hold.

features.title: Long-Call Spectral Match
features.blurb: Upload eight seconds of screaming. A 40-band acoustic model finds the gull whose scream completes yours.

features.title: Provenance-Grade Theft Ledger
features.blurb: Self-reported fry seizures don't count here. Every sandwich acquisition is timestamped and attested by two unrelated witness gulls.

demo_screen_concept: A swipeable card stack of seagull profiles: full-bleed gull portrait, name and age in summers, claimed territory ('Pier 39, north railing, held 6 yrs'), a tide-teal verified-theft badge with career sandwich count, a fake playable 8-second long-call waveform, and a screech-compatibility score out of 100. Buttons: PASS and SCREECH. A mutual match triggers a full-screen 'MUTUAL SCREECH' modal proposing a first date at the active dumpster equidistant from both territories.

images.rationale: Photo-shaped demo (dating card stack), so the budget went to three 3:4 gull profile portraits plus one 1:1 archival specimen photograph for the hero chart inset. Hero photo proper skipped because the design direction is typographic chart-editorial; testimonial headshots skipped so all three testimonials keep a consistent initials treatment.

design_direction.style: Federal nautical-chart editorial, chart-paper daylight mode. The page is staged as a Notice to Mariners issued by a heavily funded dating company that has decided the herring gull is an under-matched asset and files courtship under port operations. A flat chart-paper cream ground (#F8F4E9) runs the whole page with a faint low-alpha graticule grid; structure comes from survey-print chrome: thin navy hairline rules, section labels set as NOTICE TO MARINERS banner strips in wide-tracked caps, chart-inset panels with 2px near-square corners and double-rule frames, no shadows, no glass, no blur, no clay. The core motif is the depth contour: thin dashed navy lines that arc between sections like soundings around a shoal, with small buoy markers (a circle wearing a signal-red band) anchoring bullets, status dots, and match indicators. A compass rose sits in the hero and shrinks into section hallmarks. One signal-buoy red (#C8322B) carries the wordmark, every primary CTA, the stamped APPROVED FOR COURTSHIP block, and one word per headline; one rationed tide teal (#23726A) is reserved strictly for verified states and live telemetry (attested thefts, screech compatibility, the live perch dot) and appears nowhere else. Libre Franklin sets the wordmark and headlines in heavy municipal grotesque caps, federal-signage confident; Public Sans carries plain, faintly regulatory body copy. Every figure that pretends to be survey telemetry (decibel peaks, attested seizures, coordinates, tier prices) is set in JetBrains Mono with tabular figures inside thin-ruled paper wells, so it reads like the sounding table, not marketing. Motion is print-restrained: contour dashes march at 1px per frame, the compass needle swings once and settles on load, plates lift 2px on hover with the hairline darkening, CTAs depress 1px on press, sections fade up 6px with a 40ms stagger, all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion. No dark mode, no glass, no blur panels, no neon glow, no clay, no bento lattice, no didone engraving, no condensed athletic type, no HUD brackets, no rounded marketplace cards, no emoji. Reads like a company that files pair-bonding under 'harbor traffic' and considers the ocean a compliance surface.

design_direction.archetype: Consumer dating app staged as a federal navigational-chart notice; hero-centric landing with document chrome, feature plates as chart insets, pricing as a tariff schedule, testimonials as mariner logs.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Print-restrained: contour dashes march slowly via dash-offset, the compass needle settles once on load, plates darken their hairline and lift 2px on hover, CTAs depress 1px on press, sections fade up 6px with a 40ms stagger, all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Left column: oversized Libre Franklin caps headline with one word in signal red, sub set as a typed notice, red CTA styled as a stamped block. Right column: a chart inset with graticule, dashed depth contours, a compass rose, buoy markers labeled with fake coordinates, and a clipped archival specimen photograph of a herring gull with a mono caption plate.
